legal.draft: Draft for review: placeholders in [brackets] are the owner's to fill in, and the final text needs a legal review before launch.

s1.p: Globetrot is a trip-planning app operated by [owner: legal name and country]. Contact: [owner: contact email].

s2.p: Your account: name and email address (from your sign-up or your Google account), a hash of your password if you set one, your settings, and what you put in Globetrot: trips, stops, costs, savings amounts, lists, day plans, photos, visas, Pip requests, community posts, comments and likes. We also keep the technical records the service needs: sessions, rate-limit counters, an audit log of changes that holds field names but never personal values, and error reports (the error and its stack trace, never request bodies, headers or your account data). We do not collect your live location. Photos have their location and camera data removed before they are stored.

s3.p: To run the app you asked for: save and show your plans, calculate your savings answer, send account emails (confirmation, password reset and the emails about your free week), process payments, answer Pip, and keep the service secure and working. Under the Brazilian LGPD these uses rest on providing the service you asked for and on our legitimate interest in keeping it secure. Analytics and the Meta Pixel rely on your consent, which you can withdraw at any time.

s4.p: If you sign in with Google, we receive your name and email address from Google and use them only to create or find your account. We do not read your Google contacts, calendar, mail or Drive. Globetrot's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

s5.p: Hosting and database: Railway, [owner: region]. Email: Resend. Photo storage: [owner: provider]. Place search: Geoapify receives the text you search for and the map coordinates involved. Pip: when you ask Pip, the plan of that trip (title, dates, stops, nights, places, checklist labels, cost totals and savings amounts) is sent to DeepSeek to draft suggestions; never your name, email or other trips. Payments: Stripe, which receives your email and handles your card; we never see card numbers. Errors: Sentry, with the error and its stack trace only. Measurement: Plausible (cookieless, aggregate counts) and, only after you accept, PostHog (a few named events, no session recordings) and the Meta Pixel. Some of these providers are outside Brazil, so your data may be processed abroad under their data protection terms.

s6.p: Trips are private. Community posts are seen by everyone or only your followers, as you choose; your name, handle and Pip are shown with them. A shared route is a copy of the stops and nights at that moment, without amounts unless you chose to show them. A trip you share by link can be opened by anyone with that link: its title, stops, countries, nights, the month you leave and how far your savings are, and amounts only if you choose. Never your name or exact dates. Stopping the share ends the link for good.

s7.p: Until you delete it, or until you delete your account. Deleting the account removes your trips, photos, posts, comments, likes, follows, settings and sessions. Audit log rows stay, without personal values. Backups and error reports are kept for [owner: retention period].

s8.p: You can download everything in Settings → Your data (JSON, never passwords or tokens) and delete your account there. For anything else (correction, portability, objection, withdrawing consent, questions) write to [owner: contact email]. You can also complain to the ANPD, the Brazilian data protection authority.

s9.p: Globetrot is not meant for children under [owner: minimum age].

s10.p: We will say here, with a date, when this policy changes. Last change: [owner: date].

s1.p: Globetrot helps you plan trips: a map, days, a budget with a savings answer, lists, a passport of keepsake visas, an optional AI companion (Pip) and a community. It is offered by [owner: legal name]. Using it means you accept these terms.

s2.p: Every account starts with a 7-day free trial with no card. After it, paid plans (Explorer and Voyager) are billed monthly or yearly by our payment provider; you can cancel at any time and keep your plan until the end of the period paid. Without a plan the account becomes read-only: you can still see, export and delete your data. Extra Pip credits never expire. [owner: refund policy and the payment provider’s terms]

s3.p: Globetrot never books, sells or holds money. Costs are what you type; estimates are labelled ≈ and are not quotes. Pip’s suggestions are drafts you review; they can be wrong. Always check prices, availability and entry or visa rules on official sources. Globetrot visas and stamps are keepsakes, not documents.

s4.p: Keep your password safe; you are responsible for what happens in your account. One person per account. You can delete it at any time in Settings.

s5.p: What you post stays yours. By posting in the community you let us show it to the audience you chose, and to copy a shared route into someone’s trip when they ask. Do not post what you have no right to share, other people’s private data or live location, hate, harassment, spam or anything illegal. We may hide or remove such content and close accounts that break these rules.

s6.p: We work to keep Globetrot running and your data safe, but the service is provided as it is, without guarantees of uninterrupted availability. As far as the law allows, we are not liable for indirect losses or for decisions you make from the app’s estimates.

s7.p: We may update these terms; we will say so here with a date. These terms are governed by [owner: governing law and venue]. Contact: [owner: contact email].

why.tokyo-sensoji-dawn: Before 8 am the temple is almost empty and the incense still rises over a quiet Asakusa.
why.tokyo-tsukiji: Grilled scallops, tamagoyaki and fresh tuna from stalls that open at dawn.
why.tokyo-teamlab: Walk barefoot through rooms of light and water: a museum you step into.
why.tokyo-golden-gai: Six narrow alleys, two hundred bars with room for eight people each.
why.tokyo-daikoku: On weekend nights tuned cars gather in a highway rest area by the bay. Local tours take you there.
why.tokyo-ebisu-drift: A day trip to Fukushima to ride sideways with a drift driver at the circuit where the sport grew up.
why.tokyo-takao: An hour from the city: forest trails, a mountain temple and, on clear days, Mount Fuji.
why.tokyo-shimokita: Second-hand shops, record stores and tiny cafés where Tokyo dresses up.
why.hakone-loop: A ropeway over steaming volcanic vents, then a boat across the lake with Fuji behind.
why.hakone-onsen: A local hot spring bath in the woods, the way people from Hakone bathe.
why.hakone-openair: Sculptures in the hills and a foot bath to rest between them.
why.kyoto-fushimi-dawn: Thousands of orange gates up the mountain, and at sunrise almost nobody else on the path.
why.kyoto-kiyomizu: A wooden temple on stilts over the city, best in the late afternoon.
why.kyoto-nishiki: Five blocks of pickles, skewers and sweets that cooks in Kyoto buy every day.
why.kyoto-pontocho: A lantern-lit lane by the river with small izakaya on both sides.
why.kyoto-hozugawa: Two hours of rapids through a gorge west of Kyoto, with guides from the valley.
why.kyoto-kurama-kibune: A mountain path between two villages, ending at restaurants over a stream.
why.osaka-dotonbori: Takoyaki and okonomiyaki under the neon, the city's favourite way to eat.
why.osaka-castle: The castle and its park, with the city around the old moats.
why.osaka-shinsekai: Fried skewers in an old neighbourhood that still looks like the 1960s.
why.osaka-usj: A full day of roller coasters and the Nintendo world.
why.osaka-tenma: Covered alleys of standing bars where office workers meet after work.
why.osaka-minoo: A forest walk to a waterfall, half an hour from the centre.
why.lisbon-sintra-pena: A colourful palace on a hill in the forest, a short train ride from Lisbon.
why.lisbon-alfama-fado: Fado sung a few steps from your table in the oldest neighbourhood.
why.lisbon-tasca: Grilled sardines, bifanas and house wine where locals eat lunch.
why.lisbon-bairro-alto: Streets full of small bars where the night spills onto the pavement.
why.lisbon-ericeira-surf: A world surfing reserve an hour from Lisbon, with schools for first timers.
why.lisbon-arrabida-kayak: Clear water, cliffs and hidden coves south of Lisbon.
why.coimbra-joanina: A baroque library in gold and wood, still kept for books.
why.coimbra-fado: Coimbra's own fado, sung by students in black capes.
why.coimbra-mondego-kayak: A calm paddle down the river between villages and green hills.
why.porto-port-cellar: Cellars by the river where port wine has aged for centuries.
why.porto-livraria: A bookshop with a red staircase that looks carved.
why.porto-francesinha: Porto's sandwich under melted cheese and a beer sauce, best in a neighbourhood café.
why.porto-douro: Terraced vineyards along the river, tastings and lunch at a quinta.
why.porto-galerias: One street where Porto goes out at night, bar after bar.
why.porto-matosinhos-surf: A beginner-friendly beach at the end of the metro line.
why.ba-parrilla: Grilled beef and Malbec, the Argentine dinner.
why.ba-recoleta: A city of marble tombs, Evita's among them.
why.ba-san-telmo: Antiques, street tango and empanadas along Defensa street on Sundays.
why.ba-tango-show: Dinner and a professional tango show in a historic hall.
why.ba-milonga: Where porteños really dance tango, with a class before for newcomers.
why.ba-skydive: A tandem jump from about 3,000 metres over the flat Pampas, a day trip from the city.
why.ba-tigre-kayak: Paddle the river delta's channels, among houses on stilts.
why.colonia-barrio: Cobbled streets from the 1600s and a sunset over the river.
why.colonia-bike: A flat ride along the water to an abandoned bullring.
why.colonia-tannat: Uruguay's grape, tasted at a family winery outside town.
why.mvd-mercado: An old iron market full of grills, the heart of Uruguayan asado.
why.mvd-rambla: More than 20 km of riverside promenade, the city's living room.
why.mvd-candombe: On Sunday evenings the drum troupes parade through the old neighbourhoods.
